title: Capacity recovery retro and targeted remediations for dedicated pools after scaling regression
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-09 we observed a sustained throughput shortfall across multiple Dedicated pools for ~90 minutes during a traffic surge. Root cause analysis indicates a combination of an autoscaler threshold regression (introduced in autoscaler v2.4.1), and a change in kernel selection heuristics that increased per-request GPU memory pressure, leading to slower packing and reduced concurrency. This ticket captures a compact retro, prioritized remediation actions, and a plan to harden our recovery and verification paths for future regressions.

Impact observed:
- Median p95 latency for dedicated tenants increased 2.6x for 92 minutes.
- Several tenants hit rate limits or experienced dropped requests; 3 enterprise customers reported degraded service (support tickets opened).
- Autoscaler did not spawn the expected buffer of preemptible workers due to a threshold floor introduced in v2.4.1.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Rolled back autoscaler to v2.3.9 (2026-03-09 14:22 UTC) which restored expected scale behavior.
- Temporarily disabled the new kernel-selection flag to reduce memory pressure (2026-03-09 14:40 UTC).
- Activated emergency headroom pool for affected customers to preserve SLA for remaining 3 hours.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Produce a concise retro with timeline and definitive RCA.
2) Implement prioritized fixes to prevent recurrence (short-term hotfixes + medium-term safeguards).
3) Add automated regression detection and canarying to autoscaler and kernel-selection changes.
4) Update runbooks and on-call playbooks with clearer decision criteria and escalation flow.
acceptance_criteria: RCA documented and validated by SRE and Runtime owners
Autoscaler threshold regression reverted in CI and a test preventing the floor regression added
Kernel-selection rollback confirmed and a compatibility test added to the model onboarding pipeline
Runbook updated with precise triggers and playbook steps for headroom activation
Follow-up remediation tickets created and prioritized in the next sprint
